## Midterm 2 {#sec-midterm1}

Midterm 2 will take place on Thursday 4/30 from 7:00-9:00pm in WNS 105. This midterm will focus on content from Weeks 6-10, but some concepts from the first half of the semester will be relevant (e.g. likelihood, MLE, estimators).

You will be provided a clean version of the distribution sheet that is available on the course website.

You are allowed a **double**-sided note sheet. This note sheet may have definitions, theorems, reminders to self, etc. But you may not have any worked out examples/derivations. This note sheet will be submitted alongside your midterm.

For extra practice, additional review problems are available [here](weeks/exam/midterm2_practice_probs.pdf). Try to not look at them until after you've reviewed your notes and previous homework!

## Midterm 1

Midterm 1 will take place on Thursday 3/19 from 7:00-9:00pm in WNS 011. The first midterm will cover content through 03/13 (end of Week 5).

You will be provided a clean version of the distribution sheet that is available on the course website.

You are allowed a single-sided note sheet. This note sheet may have definitions, theorems, reminders to self, etc. But you may not have any worked out examples/derivations. This note sheet will be submitted alongside your midterm.

### Preparation

-   The best preparation you can do for the exam is to study/review, then make a draft of your note sheet. Then try some practice problems using your note sheet. Revise the sheet as needed.

    -   As you do this, you should attempt to accurately assess what topics you have mastered and which you need to practice more.

    -   As you study, it would be a good idea to compile lists of questions that you might have for Prof. Tang/the class.

-   I encourage you to re-visit and re-do previous homework problems and practice problems. Be sure to do the practice problems that we did not have time to get to in class.

-   Midterm problems will be comparable in difficulty to those assigned for homework. Some midterm problems may be similar to problems you have seen before, while others will require you to synthesize your knowledge in new ways.

### Review Problems

For extra practice, additional review problems are made available [here](weeks/exam/midterm1_review_problems.pdf). While these questions are *generally* representative of the typical scope and difficulty of individual exam questions, this review is not comprehensive, nor does it necessarily represent the expected amount of time for it will take for you to complete the exam.
